issues.description: The problem specification and solution expect Stock.findStockIngredient(String) (single-parameter). However, the template Stock.java provides findStockIngredient(String, boolean) (two parameters). This parameter mismatch prevents students from calling stock.findStockIngredient(name) as described in the task and shown in the solution, causing confusion and compilation errors when implementing SealSaloon and other logic that rely on the single-parameter method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock class provide the same method signature as in the problem specification and solution. Add or change the method to: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) { ... } (optionally keep the case-sensitive/insensitive overload). This ensures students can call stock.findStockIngredient(name) exactly as required by the exercise.

issues.description: The problem statement's class diagram defines Stock.findStockIngredient(String): StockIngredient (single-argument). The template repository's Stock implementation exposes findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) (two-argument), while the solution repository implements a single-argument findStockIngredient(String name). This mismatch in the method signature for the same conceptual operation creates confusion: students reading the diagram will expect a one-argument method, the starter code offers a different API, and the provided solution uses the one-argument form. This can cause compilation surprises and extra cognitive load mapping requirements to the template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across artifacts. Either change the template's method to a single-argument signature (public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name)) to match the problem diagram and solution, or add a single-argument overload in the template that delegates to the two-argument form (e.g., public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) { return findStockIngredient(name, true); }). Ensure the problem statement, template, and solution use the same method signature.
